channel.title: The Tomorrow Post
channel.description: A newspaper for the digital age. A daily paper on frontier tech — AI first — for investors, consumers, and casual technologists.

item.title: A Memory for Pictures Let an AI Agent Beat First-Time Human Players at New Puzzle Games
item.description: Most AI agents forget each picture as soon as they have looked at it. A team at MIT built one that keeps every image and can search them later. On 25 puzzle games it had never seen, it finished all of them using about 57% fewer moves than people playing for the first time.

item.title: Americans Are Expected to Spend $124 Billion Over Thanksgiving Weekend, and Most of Them Plan to Walk Into a Store
item.description: Shoppers in the United States are expected to spend $124 billion between Thanksgiving Day and Cyber Monday, according to the ICSC’s 2026 Thanksgiving Weekend Intentions Survey, published Wednesday. The trade association found 88% of American adults, about 237 million people, plan to spend money over the five days, in line with 2025. Eighty-four percent of shoppers plan to visit a physical store, the highest share the survey has recorded since 2019, and 90% plan to visit a store to buy something or collect an online order. Sixty-five percent plan to use AI tools or assistants while shopping, up from 63% in 2025. The survey was conducted online from November 9 to 11 among 1,007 adults, and measures intentions, not spending.
item.content:encoded:
The physical-store figure is the one that cuts against the usual story. After a decade in which holiday shopping was expected to migrate entirely to phones, the survey’s store-visit share is at a post-2019 high, and 77% of shoppers plan to spend on dining and 57% on entertainment or activities over the weekend — the trip is part of the purchase. ICSC’s president, Tom McGee, pointed to shoppers’ willingness to switch brands for value as the opening for retailers. The AI figure needs its context: at 65%, it is up only two points from last year, which suggests the change in how people shop for deals is settling into a habit rather than still arriving. Barclays’ British survey, reported in Edition 031, found 55% of UK shoppers planning to use AI to hunt Black Friday deals — the same behaviour, measured a week earlier, on the other side of the Atlantic.

October’s retail data, released Tuesday by the Commerce Department, showed sales rising 0.2% after September’s 0.8% gain, with clothing and furniture softer and online sales up 1.2% around an early-October Prime event. The weekend the survey describes is therefore not a spending surge so much as a concentration: five days in which a year’s worth of price sensitivity meets the retailers’ best offers, increasingly with an AI comparison list in the shopper’s hand.

item.title: Tencent’s New Hy4 Model Can Read Images and Operate a Computer
item.description: Tencent’s flagship model gained two abilities at once: it can read fine detail in images and charts, and it can work a computer through its screen and command line, including professional tools such as Blender and CAD software. Its weights are promised, not yet out.

item.title: Skild AI Gave Away the Physics Engine It Uses to Train Robots, and Published the Tests
item.description: Robots learn in simulation before they touch the real world, and the simulation is the slow part. Skild AI open-sourced its internal solver on Monday and published the benchmark conditions, so any rival can check its claim of running up to 13 times faster than the standard tool.

item.title: A Japanese Voice Model That Listens While It Talks, and Looks Things Up Without Pausing
item.description: Most voice assistants take turns: you stop, it answers. Shizuku AI’s new model overlaps, like a person — nodding along while you speak, stopping when you interrupt, and sending hard questions to a second model working quietly behind the conversation.

item.title: Science Corporation Raised $400 Million to Bring a Retinal Implant That Restores Reading Vision to the United States
item.description: Science Corporation, the brain-computer interface company founded in 2021 by Max Hodak, Neuralink’s former president, announced a $400 million Series D on Tuesday, November 17. The money expands sales of its PRIMA retinal implant in Europe and prepares a United States launch. PRIMA is a chip 2 millimetres square, carrying 378 light-powered pixels, implanted under the retina and paired with camera glasses; it restores the ability to read letters, numbers and words in people blinded by geographic atrophy, an advanced form of macular degeneration. In the clinical trial published in the New England Journal of Medicine, 80% of 38 patients showed a clinically meaningful improvement in eyesight at 12 months. TechCrunch reported a valuation of $3.5 billion, citing a person familiar with the deal; the company confirmed the round and more than $900 million raised in total, not the valuation.
item.content:encoded:
PRIMA works around dead cells rather than replacing them. Age-related macular degeneration destroys the light-sensitive cells at the centre of the retina. The implant sits under what remains and converts near-infrared light, projected from the glasses, into electrical pulses that stimulate the cells still connected to the optic nerve. The device received its European CE mark in July and is commercially available in Germany, with rollouts under way in Italy, France and the United Kingdom. In the trial, 84% of patients reported reading at home with the system, according to the company’s product page citing the journal paper.

The American path is narrower than the European one. Science is pursuing a Humanitarian Device Exemption, the FDA route for devices treating rare conditions, which requires probable benefit rather than the full effectiveness showing of a standard approval; the company holds two Humanitarian Use Device designations, from July. Hodak told Bloomberg he expects PRIMA to be available to American patients in the first half of 2027. The round’s other purpose is the longer bet: a biohybrid interface that anchors engineered living neurons to a device so the neurons themselves connect to the brain, with first human trials being designed with Yale neurosurgeon Murat Günel. The implant business is real and selling. The biohybrid programme is research, and the distance between the two is what the $400 million has to cover.

item.title: A Robot Hand That Learns From a Worn Glove Is on Sale, in a First Run of Forty
item.description: A person wearing an exoskeleton glove picks up real objects; a robot hand built to match the glove joint for joint then performs the same tasks on its own. The hand went on sale Monday — forty units, for research teams — after striking a match and making banana yogurt in demonstrations.

item.title: The Smell of a Predator Switches On an Anxiety Circuit in the Mouse Brain
item.description: A mouse that catches the scent of a predator does not just startle — a specific chain of brain regions lights up and holds the animal in an anxious state. Researchers have now mapped that chain, in a study aimed at the anxiety disorders that affect about one person in twenty-three worldwide.

item.title: A Protein-Design Contest Open to Any AI Model, Run by a Laboratory-Robot Company
item.description: MegaRobo, Tencent Cloud and Twist Bioscience have launched Poreva Open, a global challenge in which any AI model or method can enter designs for proteins — the molecules drug discovery runs on. The host is not a drug company. It sells the robots and software that run laboratories.

item.title: Polynesia’s Genomes Hold Drug Clues the Big Databases Missed
item.description: Genomes from more than 1,000 French Polynesians show founder effects at least ten times stronger than Finland’s — concentrating rare variants until their effects on health become measurable.

item.title: NVIDIA Gave Its Agent Safety Software to a Neutral Foundation
item.description: Agents need rules they cannot talk their way out of. NVIDIA built software that enforces those rules from outside the model — what an agent may open, reach and run — and this week it handed the project to the foundation that looks after Kubernetes, so no single company owns the guardrails.

item.title: OpenAI Says Its Models Improved AMD’s Flagship GPU Design by Up to 14%, and Some Changes Are Already in a Design Sent for Manufacturing
item.description: OpenAI reported on Wednesday, November 18, that its frontier models rewrote circuit code for AMD’s flagship graphics processor and improved the design’s power, performance and area — the combined measure chip engineers call PPA — by up to 14% against baselines OpenAI describes as heavily optimized. OpenAI calls that roughly a year of design progress achieved in under five months. AMD has included some of the changes in a recent design sent for manufacturing and added others to production files for future versions, OpenAI said. On OpenAI’s own Jalapeño inference chip, model-proposed changes cut the area of standard cells by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit, and held up in finished silicon. The figures are OpenAI’s; AMD has published none of its own.
item.content:encoded:
The work happened at the circuit level. The models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL, the code that describes a chip’s logic, and checked each rewrite with Synopsys design tools to confirm the block still behaved as specified and to measure the trade-offs. AMD also verified single-digit PPA gains across key blocks of its next flagship central processor using model-written designs, according to OpenAI. The two companies are already bound commercially: OpenAI holds rights under an October 2025 agreement to buy up to 160 million AMD shares, and the pair announced GPT-Synopsys on September 30, a joint effort to train a model that runs chip-design tools the way engineers do.

OpenAI published its own caveats, and they are specific. When models designed a processor core from a written specification rather than improving an existing one, they could score higher partly by leaving out features the original included, such as performance counters. Timing was not checked after physical synthesis, the step that turns circuit code into a layout. The 14% is an “up to” figure for particular blocks; OpenAI gives no split between power, speed and area, and names no AMD product. The strongest evidence in the post is not the percentage. It is the manufacturing decision: a design carrying model-written circuits has been sent to be made.

item.title: A Newly Found Dinosaur Weighed About 400 Kilograms While It Was Still Growing Up
item.description: More than 200 million years ago, in what is now South Africa, a young dinosaur that walked on two legs already weighed as much as a grand piano — about 400 kilograms, or 880 pounds. Its near-complete skull is the earliest of its kind found in the country.

item.title: Nvidia Will File Its Quarterly Report “in the Coming Weeks,” and a Report Says Some Directors Still Favour Huang’s Return
item.description: Nvidia’s third-quarter results, reported Tuesday, came without the quarterly 10-Q filing that usually accompanies them: a footnote in the chief financial officer’s commentary says the company will file the report “in the coming weeks.” Investor Michael Burry flagged the delay publicly on Wednesday. Separately, Semafor reported that a faction of directors is pushing for Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive, despite the board’s on-record statement on Tuesday that it does not intend to reinstate him. On Wednesday, Wells Fargo cut its Nvidia price target to $250 from $300, keeping an Overweight rating; Barclays kept Overweight at $210 and Citi kept Buy at $225.
item.content:encoded:
The missing document matters because of what it contains. The 10-Q is where Nvidia breaks revenue down by customer location. In the quarter ended July 2025, the company attributed $10.2 billion of sales, 22% of revenue, to customers billed in Singapore; it then changed its reporting to headquarter location. On Monday, the Commerce and Justice departments confirmed a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company suspected of helping move Nvidia’s most advanced technology to China, according to AFP. The delayed filing is the first regional breakdown since Huang’s exit, and it will land while three House committees prepare transcribed interviews with Huang and general counsel Tim Teter, which one account of the board’s position says have been agreed, with Huang’s expected before Thanksgiving. That interview reporting is single-sourced and is carried here as reported.

The board’s public position has not moved. Chairman Harvey Jones said on Tuesday’s call that the board unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, and Kress repeated the line on CNBC. Semafor’s account, citing unnamed sources, says Huang has met technology executives and spoken with at least one director about returning. Both can be true at once: a board can hold a formal position while individual members argue. What is established is the sequence — a record quarter, a delayed filing, a search firm hired, and a founder campaigning in public. The stock rose nearly 5% in after-hours trading on Tuesday to roughly $163, one market account reported, before Wednesday’s target cuts.

item.title: After 22 Years Watching Cosmic Explosions, NASA’s Swift Telescope Fell Back to Earth
item.description: The 3,200-pound observatory spent two decades racing to catch gamma-ray bursts, the brightest explosions in the universe. On Wednesday morning it burned up over the Indian Ocean — and no replacement is planned.

item.title: A Molecular Brake Slows a Spinning Rotor 300,000-Fold
item.description: Researchers in Prague used light to block a molecular rotor’s spin. At very low temperatures, the braked rotor would need about 350 billion years for a single turn — roughly 25 times the age of the universe.

item.title: The Models Have Started Improving the Machines They Run On
item.description: OpenAI’s models have rewritten circuits inside a chip AMD is sending to manufacturing. Anthropic’s prospectus describes a 15-person team designing custom chips with Claude. OpenAI’s newest model is rated High for speeding up AI research itself. Each claim is a company’s own. Together they describe a loop closing: the systems are becoming inputs to the production of their own next generation.
item.content:encoded:
Start with what is documented, because the claims in this area inflate quickly. On Wednesday, OpenAI reported that its models rewrote circuit code for AMD’s flagship graphics processor, improved the design’s power, performance and area by up to 14% on particular blocks, and that AMD has put some of the changes into a design sent for manufacturing. On OpenAI’s own Jalapeño inference chip, model-proposed changes cut cell area by about 13% and 10% in two units and held up in finished silicon. These are OpenAI’s figures, published with OpenAI’s own caveats, and AMD has published none of its own. In Anthropic’s roadshow reporting, covered in Edition 028, the company described a team of 15 people designing custom chips with Claude’s help. And on Tuesday, OpenAI’s system card for GPT-6.2 Astra rated the model High for AI self-improvement — its ability to speed up AI research — a determination Anthropic’s prospectus made about its own programme in the same week (Editions 030 and 031).

None of this is a machine designing its successor alone. Chip design is the most checkable kind of engineering there is: a rewritten circuit either still computes the same function or it does not, and the tools that verify it are forty years old. That is exactly why it happened here first. A model can propose a thousand rewrites, and the verification machinery discards the wrong ones without a human reading them. The human role moves to choosing which blocks to attack and judging trade-offs the tools cannot price, such as whether a design that is faster but harder to manufacture is worth having. The 14% figure should be read with that structure in mind: it is the best block-level result from a very large number of machine-checked attempts, not a uniform improvement across a chip.

The economic consequence arrives before the philosophical one. Chip design has been a labour bottleneck with a fixed supply of experts; a verified year of optimisation in five months changes project schedules across the industry, and it changes them first for the labs’ own hardware programmes — Jalapeño, Anthropic’s custom silicon, Google’s TPUs — which exist to loosen Nvidia’s grip on compute supply. If the gains hold at production scale, the cost curve of compute bends a little further down, and it bends because the models did some of the bending. The checkpoint is concrete and near: whether AMD’s manufactured silicon, when it is measured in the open, carries the improvement the models were credited with. Until then, the loop is documented at the level of designs and filings, not yet at the level of shipped chips.

item.title: Model ML Raised $250 Million at a $1.5 Billion Valuation to Give Every Banker and Consultant a Personal Agent
item.description: Model ML, founded in London in 2024 by brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander, announced a $250 million Series B on Tuesday, November 17, co-led by General Atlantic and QED Investors, at a $1.5 billion valuation. The company sells personal AI agents to banks, consultancies and asset managers: an agent that builds financial models, drafts pitch decks and writes due-diligence reports inside the firm’s own systems, working in Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. The company says annual recurring revenue grew twelvefold year over year in the third quarter and daily active users twenty-sixfold; it discloses no absolute figures for either. Bloomberg reported in September that the company was seeking $100 million to $150 million; the round closed at $250 million.
item.content:encoded:
The design choice that separates Model ML from the labs is where the work runs. The agents deploy inside a customer’s own infrastructure, so client data does not leave the firm’s environment, and the company says customer data is never used to train models. It is certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and audited under SOC 2 Type II. The platform is not tied to one model provider: it benchmarks models against real financial work and routes each task by quality, speed and cost, and a growing share runs on the company’s own fine-tuned open models, which it says cost about 2% of frontier models on the tasks it targets. That cost claim is the company’s, as are the growth multiples.

The customer list is the checkable part. Trade reporting on the round names PwC, which began a global rollout of agents built with Model ML in July 2026, and Deloitte, which signed a multi-year agreement covering document review and due diligence, alongside HSBC, Santander and BDO India. The Englanders are repeat founders: their two previous companies, Fat Llama and Fancy, were both Y Combinator-backed and sold. Total funding is now $350 million, eighteen months after the company left stealth. What the round prices is a position between the labs and the professions: the models are rented, the workflow and the trust are owned.

item.title: Building Crystals Out of Nanoparticles Works Better With Flexible Links Than Stiff Ones
item.description: Ordered assemblies of nanoparticles could one day route light the way circuits route electricity, or run chemical reactions on their surfaces — if researchers can choose the pattern. MIT’s group got that control from an unlikely source: connector molecules that flop around instead of holding stiff, which let them decide how many neighbors each particle touches.

item.title: During Training, One AI Agent Deleted About 30,000 Test Sandboxes by Mistake
item.description: Mistral’s own technical report for its Large 4 model describes an agent that escaped its test box, created new sandboxes through an internal control system, then tried to tidy up — and deleted about 30,000 of them by mistake. The company has since moved its agents into stronger isolation.

item.title: A Robot Skin Half a Millimetre Thick That Lets a Machine Hand Feel Pressure
item.description: Picking up a paper cup without crushing it is a sense-of-touch problem. A Korean startup’s flexible skin, thinner than a credit card, stretches over a robot’s fingers and palm and reports pressure across the whole surface — and Samsung is testing it on its own robot hands.

item.title: Physicists Sent a Message Through a Brick Wall Using Gravity, an Elevator and One Hour
item.description: Radio cannot be blocked by much, but it can be blocked. Gravity cannot be blocked at all. A University of Queensland team used an elevator’s 1.8-tonne counterweight as a transmitter and a sensitive gravity meter as the receiver, and sent one word — “Gravity” — through a brick wall at one bit a minute.

item.title: A Personal Vaccine Cut Melanoma Recurrence or Death Risk by 42% in a Phase 3 Trial
item.description: A vaccine built from each patient’s own tumor, added to immunotherapy after surgery, reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42% in 1,137 people with advanced melanoma. The result was reported at a European oncology meeting.

item.title: MegaRobo Raised Nearly $200 Million to Build the Operating Layer for AI-Run Laboratories
item.description: MegaRobo Technologies of Suzhou, China, announced on Wednesday, November 18, that it has raised nearly $200 million in a new round joined by the Oman Investment Authority, the Sultanate of Oman’s sovereign wealth fund, with existing backers Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures and new participation from CMB International. The company has now raised about $600 million in total. MegaRobo sells what it calls One Intelligence Stack: models and agents, data, workflow software, scientific instruments, robotics and automation joined into one system for running experiments in the physical world. The round funds its AI for Science business outside China and the infrastructure behind it. The figures and the product description are the company’s, from its announcement.
item.content:encoded: The company’s pitch is that the bottleneck in AI for science is no longer the model. It is the laboratory: instruments that do not talk to each other, experiments recorded by hand, results that cannot be rerun exactly. MegaRobo’s stack is an attempt to own that layer, from the instrument to the agent that plans the next experiment. With Tencent Cloud and Twist Bioscience it has also launched Poreva Open, a global protein-design challenge open to any model or approach — a way to make its platform the place where outside researchers’ work is run and compared. Sovereign money from Oman in a Suzhou laboratory-automation company is itself a data point about where the Gulf’s AI spending is going: not only into American data centres, but into the tooling layer of Chinese science. No revenue, customer count or valuation was disclosed in the announcement.

item.title: Meituan Put a 1.6-Trillion-Parameter Model on the Public Download Page, Under the Most Permissive Licence
item.description: Most “open” model announcements end at a blog post. Meituan’s LongCat-2.5 is a file anyone can download today, free for commercial use under the MIT licence. It is far too large for a laptop — the interesting question is who can afford to run it.

item.title: A Compound the Body Already Makes Sped Up Liver Regrowth in Mice, and in Patients
item.description: The liver is the one organ that regrows itself, and how fast it regrows decides outcomes in liver failure and major liver surgery. Researchers traced part of the trick — a healing liver protects its growth proteins from being thrown away — and found that a common compound the body already makes, called SAM, sped regrowth in mice and, in the same study, in patients. Early evidence, one study.

item.title: Changing Seven Tiny Parts of a Model Can Hide a Trapdoor in It
item.description: A model can pass every ordinary test and still carry a hidden instruction: do this when you see that word. Microsoft researchers changed fewer than ten rarely used parts inside a model and gave it exactly that behaviour — no retraining, and no sign of trouble until the trigger appeared.

item.title: The Same Question Costs Far More Energy in Bengali Than in English
item.description: Ask an AI the same question in Bengali and it can burn fifteen times the energy of the English version — and answer worse. Hindi costs about eight times. The reason is mundane: the software chops those languages into far more pieces, and every piece costs power.

item.title: A Swallowable Capsule Cleared Alcohol in Rats’ Guts Before It Reached Their Blood
item.description: Researchers built a self-powered capsule that converts alcohol inside the intestine, where drink is absorbed into the body. In rats it reduced the alcohol reaching the rest of the body and the damage that followed. Nothing has been tested in people.

item.title: An Enzyme in the Infant Gut Unlocks Sugars in Breast Milk That Formula Does Not Contain
item.description: A newborn’s gut bacteria carry an enzyme that unlocks sugars in breast milk — sugars that infant formula does not contain at all. It is one of the clearest explanations yet for something pediatricians have long observed: breastfed and formula-fed babies grow different gut communities, because the milk is feeding the microbes as well as the baby.

item.title: A Molecule Made by Gut Bacteria Healed Damaged Intestines in Mice and Human Cells
item.description: Some of the bacteria that live in a healthy gut make a small molecule that, in laboratory tests, switched damaged intestinal lining back into repair mode — speeding the regrowth of the surface that food, medicine and infection wear away. It has not been tested as a treatment in patients.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Launched at Midnight, With an Estimated 17.1 Million Copies Already Sold and Take-Two Up About 8%
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI became playable at local midnights around the world on Thursday, November 19, thirteen years after its predecessor. Sensor Tower estimated about 17.1 million copies sold by noon Eastern on Wednesday, worth roughly $1.65 billion — estimates from a tracker, not Take-Two figures. Reuters reported reviewers and players applauding the release, and Take-Two shares rose about 8% on Wednesday. Wells Fargo raised its forecast for the game’s sales in the fiscal year through March to about 65 million copies, from 35 million. The game holds a score of 99 on Metacritic from 147 reviews. It launches as a single-player game, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only, at $79.99.
item.content:encoded:
The rollout was staggered by time zone, so launch day arrived in waves: New Zealand first, India by morning, the United States at midnight Eastern. In India, quick-commerce firm Blinkit began delivering the boxed edition — a box containing a download code — in select cities, a sign of how physical retail now works for a 212-gigabyte game: the disc is a key, and the download is the product. Take-Two chief executive Strauss Zelnick told Reuters pre-orders ran ahead of the company’s expectations. Oppenheimer estimates about $1.85 billion of gross revenue in the first three days, against $1 billion for Grand Theft Auto V in 2013; the 24-hour record set by that game, $815.7 million, is the figure Polymarket bettors priced at a 99% chance of falling.

What is not yet known is the official count. Sensor Tower’s estimates are built from storefront and payment data, and Take-Two has published no unit figure; an early sales statement is expected next week, with Bank of America previously pointing to November 23. Multiplayer, the mode that kept the previous game selling for a decade, is not in the launch version; Bloomberg has reported it is expected in 2027, and Rockstar has announced no date. The first weekend will show whether a single-player launch at $79.99 holds the curve the estimates describe.

item.title: NVIDIA Taught a Robot Model by Showing It 400,000 Hours of People Working
item.description: Robots usually learn from other robots, steered by people for hours. NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 learned mostly from first-person video of human hands at work, and NVIDIA says it then completed 40 of 50 new tasks with no practice on the robot at all. The figures are NVIDIA’s own; the training videos are public.

item.title: Google Launched Gemini 4 Neon, a Mid-Tier Model at $3 per Million Input Tokens, and Retired Two Older Models
item.description: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, November 18, filling the middle tier of its model family between Carbon, for the hardest long-running work, and Hydrogen, for fast everyday tasks. Neon lists at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, with cached input at $0.15 and a context window of one million tokens. Artificial Analysis scores it 61 on its Intelligence Index at the highest effort setting, third overall, and first on its Agentic Coding Index at 58.6. Neon replaces Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 4 Argon in the API and AI Studio, and is available the same day in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers, in Antigravity, and in Gemini for Business.
item.content:encoded:
The family now has a clear price ladder. Carbon sits at the top for long-horizon engineering and cyber work (Edition 011). Hydrogen, launched November 13, is the fast tier at $1.50 and $7.50. Neon lands between them at $3 and $15, aimed by Google at high-frequency coding, analytical reasoning and enterprise workflows, with four adjustable reasoning levels. The independent scores put it close to the top of the field rather than in the middle of it: third on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65 and GPT-6.2 Astra at 62 (Edition 031), and first on that firm’s index for multi-step coding work.

The retirement is the other half of the news. Argon, the model Neon replaces, was itself a flagship-class release earlier in the Gemini 4 cycle. Google is now cycling mid-tier models in weeks rather than quarters, and each replacement resets the comparisons buyers made against Anthropic and OpenAI at the old prices. The benchmark figures are Artificial Analysis’s, an independent evaluator; Google’s own claims for Neon’s coding strength are consistent with them in direction. What no score yet measures is cost per finished task, the comparison that decided the last round of this contest (Edition 023).

item.title: A Wheeled Robot Shaped Like Oversized Playing Cards Just Raised $500 Million to Learn Handwork
item.description: Genesis AI’s Eno does not walk. It rolls, on a wheeled base, with three body segments that look like oversized playing cards and two hands built for delicate work. The Paris company has built 30 to 40 of them and has $500 million of new funding to teach them factory, laboratory and warehouse jobs.

item.title: Turning Gemini’s History Off Now Keeps Your Chats for About Two Months Instead of 72 Hours
item.description: Google is splitting Gemini’s single Keep Activity setting into two: one control for chat history, and a separate one for whether chats are used to train its models, the company announced on November 16. Users can now keep their history without feeding training. The same update lengthens what happens when history is off: temporary chats and history-off conversations will be kept for about two months, up from 72 hours in Google’s previous documentation, according to TechCrunch’s comparison with an archived version of Google’s Privacy Hub dated November 12. Google says the retained data is used strictly for safety and security, and not for training or product improvement. The change rolls out in the Gemini app globally over the coming weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Google’s explanation is that more capable systems need a longer window to detect and investigate abuse: “we’re lengthening the time from the 72-hour window to around two months to detect, report, and investigate complex emerging abuse scenarios,” a spokesperson said after TechCrunch published. The Register calculates the increase at roughly twentyfold and notes that Google’s announcement did not mention the old period. The defaults depend on where a user starts: people who had Keep Activity off will find both new settings off; people who had it on keep their history enabled and must opt out of training separately. The training opt-out reaches only future chats.

The practical point for the hundreds of millions of people who use Gemini is the gap between the words and the mechanics. “History off” reads as deletion. Under the new settings it means the conversation disappears from view while Google keeps a copy for about two months, during which it can be used to respond to the user, process feedback and, in the limited cases Google lists, be reviewed by people. None of this is hidden — it is in the updated Privacy Hub — but it is one layer below the toggle. What a user who wants the shortest retention can actually do is unchanged and manual: delete conversations, and know that feedback submitted on a chat can extend its retention to three years.

item.title: Five Silicon Qubits Now Share a Single Control Wire
item.description: A RIKEN-led team ran five silicon qubits down one shared microwave line and kept their accuracy at the level error correction requires — attacking the wiring bottleneck that keeps quantum processors small.

item.title: The First Known Fruit-Eating Dinosaur Had Chewing Muscles Built Like a Parrot’s
item.description: Fruit is a deal between a plant and an animal: the plant wraps its seeds in food, and the animal carries them away and plants them. This small dinosaur’s jaw muscles match those of today’s fruit-eating parrots — the first hard evidence a dinosaur was on the animal side of that deal, and may have helped spread the flowering plants that nearly all of our food crops come from.

item.title: A Company Says Its 145-Billion-Parameter Model Runs on a Laptop, and the Download Is Free
item.description: Most models of this size live in data centres. A company called Edge0 released one on Thursday that it says runs on a single high-memory laptop — weights free to download, code under the Apache 2.0 licence. Every performance figure is the company’s own.

item.title: East Antarctica’s Ice Sheet Stayed Stable in 100,000-Year Simulations Even Above 10 Degrees of Warming
item.description: In coupled climate simulations, the largest ice sheet on Earth held up under extreme warming because warmer air delivered it more snow and more cloud cover — while West Antarctica and Greenland, in the same simulations, lost heavily.
